newsitem.title: USA: UPS in talks with White House on strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS in talks with White House on strike.

text.p: United Parcel Service's chief negotiator in contract talks with the Teamsters union said on Monday the company was in discussions with the White House over the Teamsters strike that began early today.
"We do have people discussing it with the administration," the negotiator, Dave Murray, told Cable News Network.
Asked if there was any word that President Clinton would get involved, Murray said, "Not that I know about."
The White House has been keeping close tabs on the negotiations, but spokesman Barry Toiv said earlier that Clinton did not plan to intervene at this time.

"At this time, the administration does not believe that the standard for intervention under the Taft-Hartley Act has been met," Toiv said, referring to the federal law under which the White House may intervene.
Immediately after the talks broke down, Labor Secretary Alexis Herman issued a statement calling on the two sides to go back to the bargaining table and avoid disruption to the public.
"UPS and Teamsters representatives should press on and not rest until they find the common ground that resolves this dispute with the least disruption," Herman said.
UPS, the biggest U.S. shipping company, handles 12 million packages a day and employs 301,000 people in the United States, 185,000 of whom are represented by the Teamsters.
